chose: The screen a `left` opens next is an optional `next` on the existing `left` case of the engagement event, not a new event or pipeline. A move within an affordance names the place (`decide`). A screen closing names the place that comes on screen next in the same turn of the event loop, with its affordance, as `<affordance>.<place>` (`today.today`), through one hand-off every places runtime shares; registry ids never hold a dot, so the two forms can't be confused. A flat affordance id was tried first and refused by the registry's own data: places `reading`, `finish` and `lesson` share ids with sibling affordances, and place ids are stable for good. `next` is left out, never guessed, when the app went to the back, when nothing naming a place comes on that turn, or when the next screen is another pipeline's. Home accepts the field on `left` only, as a name from the app's code; the phone checks it against the registry.
options: `next` on `left`: own place, or `<affordance>.<place>` of the pipeline, via a same-turn hand-off (chosen)
`next` as a flat id: own place or sibling affordance id (refused: ids collide in the registry)
the route path entered, read from the router as the screen unmounts
gray: How the app names where the owner went is a shape a later story builds on (taps per step, other flows); the same-turn hand-off can miss a screen that mounts after a load, which reads as unknown rather than wrong.
undo: Record a call that moves this one, and change `stepPlace`, the hand-off and `checkEvent`'s `next` rule with their tests; kept events keep the field as sent.
